first_message: Updates are taking much longer than usual. The shared cluster that lets our applications locate one another is in poor health. Credential delivery is sluggish too, and numerous backend applications rely on that infrastructure. Typical key-value updates are taking a couple of seconds rather than a fraction of one, and a single host has elevated processor utilization. Members are falling behind on updates, the primary keeps losing synchronization with voting peers, and downstream applications are failing health assessments.

first_message: People can't open their code projects. It's our online workspace for software teams, running on Postgres with a main instance paired with a live replica. Earlier, lots of customers couldn't submit discussion replies on tickets or proposed code changes; now the platform is down. Our replica lagged until synchronization ceased because the transaction logs it needed were no longer on the main server. Fresh database copying attempts seemed to stall, one reported a shortage of replication slots, and after a configuration change the database initially failed to start due to excessive semaphore allocation.

Users say the page will not load. Our automated software integration system is affected. People cannot open the dashboard or launch build jobs. Several services are performing poorly, and fewer event callbacks are reaching us from the repository host.
